title: Accusative and Dative Prepositions
definition: German prepositions determine the grammatical case of the noun or pronoun that follows. Some always take the accusative, some always take the dative, and two-way prepositions use accusative for direction and dative for location.

rules.title: Prepositions that always take the accusative
rules.explanation: Memorize durch, für, gegen, ohne, and um. The following noun or pronoun takes the accusative.

examples.german: Das Geschenk ist für meinen Bruder.
examples.english: The gift is for my brother.
I am coming without my key.

rules.title: Prepositions that always take the dative
rules.explanation: Memorize aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, and zu. The following noun or pronoun takes the dative.

examples.english: I am at my friend's place.

examples.german: Ich wohne seit einem Jahr hier.
examples.english: I have lived here for one year.

examples.german: Das Geschenk ist von meinem Vater.
examples.english: The gift is from my father.
I am going to the doctor.

rules.title: Two-way prepositions
rules.explanation: An, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, and zwischen can take either case. Use dative for location (wo? where?) and accusative for destination or direction (wohin? where to?).

examples.german: Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch.
examples.english: The book is on the table.

examples.german: Ich lege das Buch auf den Tisch.
examples.english: I put the book onto the table.
We are going into the kitchen.

rules.title: Prepositions with pronouns
rules.explanation: Use the correct case form of personal pronouns after the preposition.

examples.note: ohne takes accusative; context determines sie.

common_mistakes.explanation: Für takes accusative; masculine mein becomes meinen.

common_mistakes.wrong: Das Buch liegt auf den Tisch.
common_mistakes.correct: Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch.
common_mistakes.explanation: Location (wo?) uses dative with a two-way preposition.

common_mistakes.wrong: Ich lege das Buch auf dem Tisch.
common_mistakes.correct: Ich lege das Buch auf den Tisch.
common_mistakes.explanation: Destination (wohin?) uses accusative with a two-way preposition.

memorization_list.german: aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu

memorization_list.english: where? — location, dative with two-way prepositions
where to? — destination, accusative with two-way prepositions

mastery_goal: You can group common prepositions by case and choose dative or accusative correctly in simple location and direction sentences.
